title: Rav Yosef ben Chuni, an Amora
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Sanhedrin 105b preserves the valuable saying Hyman ascribes to him: “A person envies everyone except his son and his student.” Hyman cites Sotah 47a for a statement by R”Y bar Chuni that Ruth was a granddaughter of Eglon, king of Moab. But he says the name there should read R’ Yose bar Chanina, as the teaching is attributed in Nazir 23b

notes.text: The abbreviated ב״ב does not specify maternal descent. Sotah47a currently has Yose ben Chuni saying Ruth was Eglon’s daughter, Eglon being Balak’s son; Nazir23b has Yose bar Chanina saying she was Eglon’s son’s daughter. Hyman’s notice gives granddaughter and proposes the Nazir attribution. The genealogy and name differences remain open.

No new primary scalar was supplied for this notice. The earlier Sotah 47a and Nazir 23b consultations are inherited, not newly read here: Yose ben Chuni versus Yose bar Chanina, and daughter versus son's daughter, were recorded separately. Hyman's ב״ב remains granddaughter without imposing maternal descent. His instruction that the name SHOULD READ Yose bar Chanina remains an attributed correction, not an accepted name replacement or a genealogy repair. Heading Rav Yosef is not silently equated with Yose or Yochanan. The final Horayot citation continues the sentence across units; the supplied terminal semicolon is retained.

In the consulted Sanhedrin 105b the saying on envy is attributed to Rav Yosei bar Chuni, where Hyman’s heading names Rav Yosef. The consulted Sotah 47a calls Ruth a daughter of Eglon, son of Balak, and attributes the statement to Rabbi Yosei ben Chuni. Nazir 23b and Horayot 10b name Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, and make Ruth the daughter of Eglon’s son. Horayot 10b also calls Eglon the son of Balak’s son. The distinct genealogy statement in Sanhedrin 105b is attributed to Rabbi Yosei bar Huna. These readings leave Hyman’s proposed correction and the relationship among the names open.
